question.text: Sulphuryl chloride $\left(\mathrm{SO}_{2} \mathrm{Cl}_{2}\right.$ ) reacts with white phosphorus $\left(\mathrm{P}_{4}\right)$ to give

solution.text:
When sulphuryl chloride $\left(\mathrm{SO}_{2} \mathrm{Cl}_{2}\right)$, reacts with white phosphorus $\left(\mathrm{P}_{4}\right),$ it give phosphorus pentachloride $\left(\mathrm{PCl}_{5}\right)$ and sulphur dioxide $\left(\mathrm{SO}_{2}\right)$. The reaction is as follows:
$$
\mathrm{P}_{4}+10 \mathrm{SO}_{2} \mathrm{Cl}_{2} \longrightarrow 4 \mathrm{PCl}_{5}+10 \mathrm{SO}_{2}
$$
